title: The Ledger of Nagasaki's harbor
premise: In the waning days of a war that has already decided Nagasaki's fate, Xanthe Zhou, a nurse of mixed heritage working in a harbor-side field workshop, keeps a secret ledger of the dead and disappeared whose names military reports erase. When an officer's aide abandons a child at her door with orders to forget, Xanthe realizes the boy is evidence of something the garrison will burn to bury—including the workshop itself. Torn between Major Ishikawa Renjiro, who offers protection at the price of silence, and the smuggler Aya, who offers love at the price of danger, Xanthe must choose what can be carried when the evacuation order comes. In the end, Xanthe sends the ledger and the child out on Aya's boat while staying behind to hold the records together, surviving the firestorm only because the names she saved are remembered by those who escaped.
about_author: Noor Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in coastal port cities. Their fiction explores the quiet paperwork of history—the ledgers, manifests, and unsent letters through which ordinary people resist being forgotten.

chapters.title: What the Orders Omit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the crowded harbor workshop, Xanthe treats the wounded while secretly recording names the officers' reports leave blank—deserters, foreign laborers, the unclaimed. The emotional beat is weary vigilance: she measures everything by what fits in a satchel. When Major Ishikawa notices her careful hands but not her ledger, tension hums beneath his courtly attention.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An officer's aide leaves a mute boy on the workshop step with money and one instruction: forget the face. Xanthe recognizes the boy as the son of a name already inked in her ledger—a man listed as a traitor. The beat is dread blooming into resolve; for the first time, invisibility feels like complicity, and Aya the smuggler offers a dangerous way out.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Aya POVs. Ishikawa discovers the missing child and offers Xanthe protection if she surrenders the ledger; his corruption is tender, almost sincere. Aya readies her boat but demands Xanthe come too. Climax: soldiers torch the records office early, and Xanthe races through smoke to save the ledger, choosing the names over both safety and Ishikawa's bargain.

chapters.title: Carried Out on the Tide
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, then a coda from the grown boy decades later. Wounded but alive, Xanthe puts the ledger and the child aboard Aya's boat and stays behind to misdirect the search party, trusting love to return for her. Resolution: the boat slips past the burning harbor; the coda reveals the ledger preserved, its names spoken aloud, and Xanthe found alive among the survivors—belonging, at last, to no order but her own.
